name: Finish the Line Karaoke
why_it_works: An unfinished pattern is almost painful to leave. Lyrics on screen with a bouncing highlight let viewers sing along, then the last word drops out and their brain sings it for them. That small win drives replays and duets.

hook.pattern: Show the karaoke lyric bar and dare the viewer to finish the last word before it appears.
examples: Sing the last word. Bet you already know it.
Finish this lyric before the beat comes back.
Duet this if you can finish the line.

variables.name: song_title
variables.description: Original song title, which is also the missing last word (1-3 syllables)

variables.name: line_one
variables.description: First lyric line, capitalized, one breath, 8 syllables or fewer, ending on the sound the title rhymes with
variables.example: You kept me up through the night

variables.name: line_two
variables.description: Second lyric line, capitalized, 7 syllables or fewer, stopping one word before the title

variables.name: listen_link
variables.description: Where to hear or buy it, 4 words or fewer

visual.prompt: Artist-supplied vertical photo of {{artist_name}} holding a mic toward the camera, moody purple and teal stage light

beats.purpose: karaoke line one with bouncing highlight
line two stops before the title word
silent gap for viewer to sing
reveal title word plus where to hear it

visual.prompt: Real performance footage of {{artist_name}} singing the final word, lights blooming on the downbeat, vertical crop

cta: Duet this and finish the line. Full song '{{song_title}}': {{listen_link}}.

music.feel: half-time R&B pop, sparse keys, deep kick

slides.headline: Finish the line
slides.visual_prompt: Bold title slide, {{artist_name}} name in big type, karaoke-style lyric bar graphic, dark background with neon accent

slides.headline: Line one
slides.visual_prompt: Lyric slide, white words on black, first word highlighted in neon like a karaoke bounce

slides.headline: Line two
slides.visual_prompt: Lyric slide, highlight stops one word short, a blank glowing underline where the last word goes

slides.headline: {{song_title}}
slides.body: That's the one. You sang it before you read it.
slides.visual_prompt: Cover-art style slide with {{song_title}} in large type over an artist-supplied photo of {{artist_name}}

slides.headline: Why your brain knew it
slides.body: Line one ends on a sound, the title rhymes with it, and it lands on beat one. Your ear predicts the rhyme.
slides.visual_prompt: Simple diagram slide, the two lyric lines with the rhyming sounds circled and beat numbers above

slides.headline: Write your own ending
slides.body: Stitch this with your own last word. We ask before using any fan line, and credit you by name.
slides.visual_prompt: Blank lyric card with a pen and a glowing empty underline, dark background, neon accent

slides.headline: Hear it now
slides.visual_prompt: Clean end card with {{artist_name}} name and a play-button icon

craft.notes: Title placement: the title is the last word of the couplet and the end-rhyme partner of line one, so the ear predicts it (night / daylight). Keep each sung line to one breath, about 8 syllables. Stress the final syllable before the title on beat 4 so the title lands on the next beat 1, then cut the audio for exactly one beat. Tempo/feel: 80 BPM, half-time pop or R&B, sparse keys and a deep kick so the silence feels intentional.

do_not: Use someone else's lyrics, even a famous line people would know
Make the missing word guessable only if you already know the song
Let the highlight run ahead of the vocal; viewers lose the sing-along
Generate an AI version of the artist's face or voice; use real photos and footage
compliance: Fan duets and submitted lines: get a written release before reusing any fan's video, voice or lyric in the song or in ads
Credit every fan line used by name or handle, and say up front whether submissions can be used commercially and whether any pay applies
Photos and performance footage of the artist are real and artist-supplied; no AI likeness or voice clone
